sense.text: Before the class turns to its subject, it turns to the fires in California, and it opens there: “Rejoice not when thine enemy falleth, and let not thine heart be glad when he stumbleth”. This is about the enemy of your people. The Bible says do not be glad when he stumbles.

precepts.why:
Job says it the same way: “If I rejoiced at the destruction of him that hated me, or lifted up myself when evil found him”. That shows we are not supposed to do that.

“Neither have I suffered my mouth to sin by wishing a curse to his soul.” That is to the Israelites out there who are wishing death on us and on our families. The Most High hears all the evil you are speaking, and he is going to get you. We pray for them and ask the Lord to forgive them. But to those in the camps, the followers: judgment is going to come on you too, because you hear the evil and you are complicit with the evil.

sense.text:
There are angels that control fire. Many have never been taught this in their churches, and it is a shock to the system, but here it is: “And another angel came out from the altar, which had power over fire”. This angel had power over fire.

What we saw in California, the brother who stood in his burned house after twenty-five years, the sister left with only the clothes on her back, the neighbourhood that looks like a war zone, is devastating, a sad reality. But fire is in the hands of the Lord: there is an angel that has power over fire.

precepts.why: “And of the angels he saith, Who maketh his angels spirits, and his ministers a flame of fire.” His angels are spirits, and his ministers are a flame of fire.

Isaiah 29 in its context is the destruction that is going to take place in the land of Israel, but there is one precept to take notice of in verse 6: “Thou shalt be visited of the Lord of hosts with thunder, and with earthquake, and great noise, with storm and tempest, and the flame of devouring fire.”

That is the Lord that does that. The church is not going to tell you that; the church don't know that. The churches out there are dumb as hell. Anytime there is a fire, those are the spirits of the Lord, the Lord's angels doing it.
“For the congregation of hypocrites shall be desolate, and fire shall consume the tabernacles of bribery.” Fire shall consume the tabernacles of bribery.
“The voice of the Lord divideth the flames of fire.” The Lord always dealt with fire.

There is much more, but it ends with this one: “As the fire burneth a wood, and as the flame setteth the mountains on fire; So persecute them with thy tempest, and make them afraid with thy storm.” The fire in the woods and on the mountains, the tempest and the storm, are the Lord persecuting and making afraid.

sense.text:
In these last days people are worried about Trump being in office, and that project of his. There is no worry here. Bring it on: we want that to happen. A lot of people are afraid of Trump being in office because they say tribulation is going to come, and our people want to stay in the United States of America forever. No, we are not meant to be here forever.

“I will go and return to my place, till they acknowledge their offence”: this is what the Lord is waiting for, till we acknowledge our offences. “And seek my face”: to seek his face means study the Bible, learn who you are. “In their affliction they will seek me early”: in the affliction of our people, our race.

So what we saw on the news with the brother and the sister whose homes were burned, there is a reason behind it. It is meant to cause our people to repent. Our people say, God don't care about me, to hell with it, and walk off. No. The Most High has things that we look at and say, this is terrible, why did God allow that? There is a divine purpose behind it: to get us all to repent of our sins.

The last man standing is a phrase used for a situation where all the participants have been eliminated or defeated and only one remains, in a conflict or a challenge where the goal is to last, or to outperform your former self. You are not here to outperform your brother or your sister. You are here to outperform your former self, that former man or woman still inside of you that raises its head up once in a while. We are in this thing together. To outperform your former self is the ability to withstand challenges and emerge victorious.

“Watch ye therefore, and pray always, that ye may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that shall come to pass, and to stand before the Son of man.” That is a heavy thing Christ said: see the word worthy. Every man and every woman in this room is one of a thousand, but that one of a thousand has to endure to the end. We have all been called into this truth, but you are only chosen when you endure to the end.

precepts.why:
“In a dream, in a vision of the night, when deep sleep falleth upon men, in slumberings upon the bed; Then he openeth the ears of men, and sealeth their instruction”. When we are asleep, that is when God opens our minds to his instructions and seals them.

“That he may withdraw man from his purpose, and hide pride from man.” Your purpose may be, I am going to work at 7:30, get there early, and do A, B and C; but the Lord says, I have something else, and you get up the next morning with another thought. And he hides pride from man, because man has pride. “He keepeth back his soul from the pit, and his life from perishing by the sword”: from death, from being put to death.

Then the chastening: “He is chastened also with pain upon his bed”, “So that his life abhorreth bread, and his soul dainty meat”: you are in such a bad state you cannot eat. “His flesh is consumed away”: you get smaller and smaller, and “his bones that were not seen stick out.” “Yea, his soul draweth near unto the grave, and his life to the destroyers.”

“If there be a messenger with him, an interpreter, one among a thousand”: an interpreter of God's word. That is where the brothers come in, and the sisters fall in line with that too: we are interpreters of the scriptures. “To shew unto man his uprightness”: where you should be and where you have gone wrong in your life. “Then he is gracious unto him, and saith, Deliver him from going down to the pit: I have found a ransom.” The ransom is Christ.

The brother we saw who was upset with God needs to hear the word. Bad things happen to us to cause us to repent, to turn from our wicked ways and turn towards God. But people say, I'm righteous, I'm good, I'm holier than thou.

“Behold, this have I found, saith the preacher, counting one by one, to find out the account: Which yet my soul seeketh, but I find not: one man among a thousand have I found”. Solomon found one man among a thousand that sought after God. “But a woman among all those have I not found.” Solomon had a thousand women, and out of all of them not one sought after the Lord.

So it is a rarity when a sister comes into God's truth, because usually they want to be water baptized, washed in the blood of the Lamb, roll around on the floor and foam at the mouth, and commit adultery with the preacher. That is where the majority of our sisters are, in these churches.

“For there shall be in every place, and in the next cities, a great insurrection upon those that fear the Lord.” What we saw with the brother and the sister who lost their homes, we pray the Most High be merciful to them, but things are going to escalate towards our people.

“They shall be like mad men, sparing none”: the nations are going to be like madmen; they are not going to spare the Israelites, our twelve tribes. “But still spoiling and destroying those that fear the Lord”: they want to destroy those that fear the Lord. “For they shall waste and take away their goods, and cast them out of their houses.”

“Then shall they be known, who are my chosen”: if we can endure to the end through that, then it shall be known who are his chosen, because that man and that woman will have kept the faith. “And they shall be tried as the gold in the fire.”

sense.text:
When something bad happens you have three choices: you can let it define you, you can let it destroy you, or you can let it make you durable. The three Ds: define, destroy, durable. You have to pick which one.

When you let bad things define you: “Give not over thy mind to heaviness, and afflict not thyself in thine own counsel.” Sometimes bad things happen and you let that destroy your world, or things do not go the way you planned and you let that define you, and everything is wrong.

It causes low self-esteem, a negative self-image: negative self-talk, focusing on your flaws and exaggerating imperfections, feeling unworthy or inadequate, avoiding challenges, hesitant to take risks out of self-doubt. When you let a bad situation define you, you do not see yourself in a good light. You run from situations, because you feel you can't do it, you can't overcome, you just ain't right, you're no damn good.

precepts.why:
When it defines you, it also limits your growth. “And the Spirit of God came upon Zechariah the son of Jehoiada the priest, which stood above the people, and said unto them, Thus saith God, Why transgress ye the commandments of the Lord, that ye cannot prosper?” See that: why transgress ye, that ye cannot prosper. “Because ye have forsaken the Lord, he hath also forsaken you.” When we go against the Lord, he will forsake us, and things will go wrong.

It also brings fear and anxiety, making a person hesitant to take risks or to step out of their comfort zone and try new things. When we go to camp we see which brothers are fearful: scared to stand before an audience, thinking somebody is going to punch them in the face, with no confidence in their speaking.

Letting a bad situation define you also affects your work life. “A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches, and loving favour rather than silver and gold.” A good name means a good reputation. You want a good reputation in this truth; you want to build up your character.

Bad situations, conflicts with co-workers, a toxic work culture or personal stress lead to decreased productivity, increased stress, burnout and low morale. We see it in here: when we ask certain brothers or sisters to do things and their productivity goes lower and lower, we know something is going on in your spirit.

It also affects your relationships. “He that troubleth his own house shall inherit the wind: and the fool shall be servant to the wise of heart.” When you let things define you and you can't overcome them, it will affect your relationship, your marriage.

“Unless a man hold himself diligently in the fear of the Lord, his house shall soon be overthrown.” It affects your relationships and your marriage. Bad situations bring conflict and tension, disagreements and friction; they erode trust (there were something like eight cases of adultery in the past two weeks); they bring emotional distance and isolation, where a person withdraws and cannot open up or be present for their loved ones; they bring stress, and they hinder communication. There is a lot of that going on.

sense.text: The second choice: you can let a bad situation destroy you. “Whoso despiseth the word shall be destroyed”. As the scripture says, do nothing without counsel. Some brothers and some sisters despise counsel, so they go off on a tangent on their own; they despise the word. Then when something really bad happens they want us to fix it, and it is too late. We can't fix it.

precepts.why:
“And it was revealed in mine ears by the Lord of hosts, Surely this iniquity shall not be purged from you till ye die, saith the Lord God of hosts.” That is some of you brothers and sisters who just love adultery: you can't stop it, you just got to have somebody's wife, somebody's husband. God tells you this is going to make you stop.

Some of you are fornicators like you wouldn't believe, and you keep on, and the Lord being merciful with you is the reason you are still breathing. But there is going to come a day, an hour and a minute when all hell is going to break loose, and then you will ask what the hell is going on. And then you can either lie about it or confess it.

sense.text: This is still letting bad situations destroy you. “For of heaviness cometh death”: that heaviness is depression. Of depression comes death; death is coming. “And the heaviness of the heart breaketh strength”: the heaviness of the heart is the depression of the mind, and it breaks your spiritual strength, which leads to your physical breaking. Sometimes we go through health issues, and that man or that woman refuses to try to increase their physical strength and their spiritual strength.

“In affliction also sorrow remaineth”: when you are afflicted, sorrow remains, like the brother and the sister we saw in California; their sorrow is going to remain for quite a while, till their situation is fixed. “And the life of the poor is the curse of the heart”: being poor will make you rob, steal and kill.

As we go through these scriptures, apply them to yourself. Don't think this class isn't pertaining to you. This class is for you.

“Take no heaviness to heart”: these bad situations happen; do not take them to heart. “Drive it away”: when you have that spirit of depression and sorrow, God says drive it away. “and remember the last end”: remember the end, because sorrow will break bones. It will break you.

The third choice: you can let that bad situation make you durable. Durable means able to withstand wear, pressure or damage: hard-wearing, long-lasting, heavy duty, tough, resistant, strong. A bad situation can make you strong. A bad situation can make you long-lasting. A bad situation can make you durable.

“And not only so, but we glory in tribulations also”: that is the spiritual man and the spiritual woman. It sounds almost crazy: who rejoices in tribulation? That is the afterthought. Once you sit back and the smoke clears, now you can rejoice: I thought I'd never get through that thing.

“Knowing that tribulation worketh patience”: only the spiritual man and woman know that tribulation works patience. It is teaching you something. God is trying to teach us all patience.

“And patience, experience”: patience gives us experience, because a lot of us lack experience in this walk. Sure, you have experience in the world, but that is not what God is talking about; he is talking about your experiences in this truth. “And experience, hope”: experience will teach you and give you hope.

“And hope maketh not ashamed”: once you have that hope you will never be ashamed, because you know you will come through it in the end, “because the love of God is shed abroad in our hearts by the Holy Ghost which is given unto us.”

precepts.why:
Because Romans 5 sounds crazy, see what Christ says speaking through Paul: “Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous”. He understood that. It sure ain't joyous. “But grievous”: grievous as hell. You lose your house, your health, your mother, your father, your son, your daughter, your job: it is very grievous.

“Nevertheless afterward”: that is it right there, afterward. “It yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.” The spiritual man and the spiritual woman are exercised in the word of God, to understand: I went through A, B and C because of D, E, F and G. What doesn't kill you makes you stronger. That is the afterthought of Romans 5.

sense.text: “Furthermore we have had fathers of our flesh which corrected us, and we gave them reverence”. We all had fathers in the flesh, most of whom beat the hell out of us, and we still reverenced our fathers. “Shall we not much rather be in subjection unto the Father of spirits, and live?” Christ is saying through Paul: isn't it better to submit yourself to the Father of spirits and live? The chastisement the Lord puts on us is to give us that kind of life: eternal life.

“For they verily for a few days chastened us after their own pleasure”: your parents chastened you for a few days. They beat you and put you on punishment, timeout: no TV for a week, no video games, you ain't going outside with your friends.

“But he for our profit”: God for our spiritual profit, our benefit, “that we might be partakers of his holiness.” There is a divine purpose behind it.

“Now no chastening for the present seemeth to be joyous, but grievous”: you are crying like hell when things go wrong. Some brothers have lost a loved one, and that hurts; some of your spouses bounced on you, and that hurts for a moment. “Nevertheless afterward it yieldeth the peaceable fruit of righteousness unto them which are exercised thereby.”

“Wherefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the feeble knees”. Christ is saying: get yourself together. Shake that spirit of depression. Your hands are down and your knees are bent, and he says straighten your back, lift up your hands, send up those prayers. Strengthen those feeble knees, instead of, oh, I can't do it.

precepts.why:
“Strengthen ye the weak hands”: that is the depressed brother, the depressed spirit, the sister who can't get over nothing. “And confirm the feeble knees.” “Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not”: we have to tell each other that, be strong. “Behold, your God will come with vengeance, even God with a recompence; he will come and save you.”

Those are words of comfort, words of strength that men and women need when they are going through their trials and tribulations. God doesn't give the hardest battles to his toughest soldiers; he creates the toughest soldiers through life's hardest battles. When you go through hard times it is meant to build you, to strengthen you, so that you can build the strength of the next man or woman going through something similar or worse: I've been there, I can help you with A, B and C.

sense.text: “But they also have erred through wine, and through strong drink are out of the way; the priest and the prophet have erred through strong drink”. The strong drink and the wine are philosophies, religions and politics. “They err in vision, they stumble in judgment.”

“For all tables are full of vomit and filthiness, so that there is no place clean.” Whatever religion you decide to go into, whatever political group you decide to go into, God says there is vomit there.

The people going from table to table are looking for knowledge, and that is why it says all tables are full of vomit. Then: “Whom shall he teach knowledge? and whom shall he make to understand doctrine?” Who is God going to show and make understand his doctrine? “Them that are weaned from the milk, and drawn from the breasts.”

To get the knowledge and the understanding you have to be on his word the way a baby sucks his mother's breast milk. How often does a baby suck? Not once a day: morning, noon, night and in between. If you want to get strong, if you want help, if you want to escape from the vomit of this world, you have to be in this Bible learning it like a baby at his mother's breast.

“For precept must be upon precept, precept upon precept; line upon line, line upon line; here a little, and there a little”. Here he teaches us how to read the Bible, to gain the understanding of his mysteries, his knowledge, his doctrine.
“For with stammering lips and another tongue will he speak to this people”: the languages we all speak are these bastard languages.

“This is the rest wherewith ye may cause the weary to rest”: to cause the weary to rest, teach them precept upon precept, line upon line, here a little and there a little. “And this is the refreshing”: the refreshing to your soul. “Yet they would not hear”: our people refuse to hear.

“For the eyes of the Lord are upon them that love him”: the Lord is watching us. “He is their mighty protection and strong stay, a defence from heat, and a cover from the sun at noon, a preservation from stumbling, and an help from falling.” The Lord is a help from falling.

But pay close attention to what it says: them that love him. If you love me, keep my commandments. Some people get sick, and when they get a little better they don't come to the school; they get Sabbath sick. Sunday through Friday you were good, but here is the Sabbath. Didn't God just heal your black behind? And this is how you repay the Lord? Some of you got delivered from a bad court situation, and now that you are delivered we don't see you no more. You stupid, dumb as hell: you don't know that something else bad can happen. There was a brother who couldn't stand us and showed up once every three moons, until he got caught up in a court situation: can y'all pray for me, can you anoint me? He got delivered, and where is he now? Our people don't learn.

“He raiseth up the soul, and lighteneth the eyes”: to lighten the eyes is to enlighten your spiritual eye. “He giveth health, life, and blessing.” The Lord is the one that gives health, life and blessing.

precepts.why:
Christ said the same about being healed and being warned: “Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee.” A lot of y'all only come here when something is wrong. We pray over you, we anoint you, and as soon as you get better you go back to your wickedness, and you don't understand that you made your situation worse. Christ said a worse thing is going to happen to you than what you came to us for help for.

Some will use the church and then go about their way, and don't realize they are going to pay. It is like the fornicators and adulterers: we put you out for a couple of months, bring you back, and you do the same foolishness again. When your rod blows up one night, we can't help you then.

sense.text: “Before I was afflicted I went astray: but now have I kept thy word.”
“Thou art good, and doest good; teach me thy statutes.” That is the mentality we all have to have: teach me thy statutes.

“The proud have forged a lie against me”. When you are in this truth, people will lie on you. If it ain't your mama (some of your mothers hate the truth), they say you are in a cult, he beats women, whatever it is: a whole litany of lies from family, friends and foes.

If you ain't got no enemies, you better go out and find some. When you are doing the right thing, people will lie on you and slander you. It is not if, it is when. “But I will keep thy precepts with my whole heart.”
“Their heart is as fat as grease; but I delight in thy law.” The Bible says their heart is as fat as grease; that is what God says.

“It is good for me that I have been afflicted; that I might learn thy statutes.” That is the mentality we have to have when we go through tough times: after we come through it, say it is good for me that I have been afflicted. You don't realize that when you are going through tough times you get into the Bible more than you have ever been, because you are searching for the true God: enlighten me, show me what to do, what to say, how to get out of this situation, forgive me if there is some sin involved.

precepts.why:
“A wicked doer giveth heed to false lips; and a liar giveth ear to a naughty tongue.” Some of the camps out there are a bunch of liars. One woman says the school wanted her to be a surrogate wife, at fifty-five years old: this is foolishness, this is madness.

You can't come to anybody up here with foolishness. We are going to say, no, that's a lie: do you have any evidence? No? You're a liar, get out of here with that. But a wicked man, a liar, will entertain that stuff.

Three women came into a Clubhouse room to lie on one of the men here, about a sister ten years ago who took the money the church raised for her schooling and went off. Now they say her man was beating her and we are responsible. When was this beating taking place? You said nothing to nobody; now ten years later your life is a mess, the money is spent, nobody cares about you, and you see this man has moved on and is happy, so you want to start a lie. That's how women are. It is an evil world we live in.

This goes back to the liar: “If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen? And this commandment have we from him, That he who loveth God love his brother also.” That is something we, blacks and Latinos, really have to apply.

“A lie is a foul blot in a man, yet it is continually in the mouth of the untaught.” If you are untaught, unlearned, you will continually lie.

The lies: that the Bishop killed the ex-Elder; that when we first went to Ghana we had sex with little African boys; that he had sex with his uncles; the newest, from the fat camp, that he did homosexual stuff in college; that he forced the last school to eat pork; a fake website saying he has a hundred and fifty million dollars, or four million. Monopoly money, and his son still has to work a job. Somebody took the time to make a fake website, and Black Hebrew Israelites are repeating it; even an apologist said, I heard. You didn't hear nothing: you got it from a fake. Where are they getting this stuff from? The devil.

sense.text:
No matter what you go through in life, brothers and sisters, no matter how hard or how bad, be reminded of this. Sometimes when you are going through bad things you think you are the only one in the world, that nobody knows or understands. “There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man: but God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able”. God knows all of our breaking points. He will not allow you to be tempted above what you are able; he gives Satan guidelines and parameters.

“But will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it.” The way to escape: number one is the scriptures. Number two, you have friends and family, brothers and sisters in this truth you can talk to: my mind is preoccupied with this sin, let's go over some scriptures, let's hang out. It might be a pull back to drug use, to alcohol, to some hoochie mama's house; and the Most High has that phone ring, and it's a brother: let's go hang out somewhere. That is the Most High giving you a door to escape while the home girl was right there at the door. You either take the way to escape or you don't. It's up to you.

“Beloved, think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you, as though some strange thing happened unto you”. Why am I going through this, why are bad things happening to me? Because God is trying to build you. He is trying to make you into a soldier, to build you mentally and spiritually, to teach you patience, experience and hope. That is what the spiritual man and woman have to see; don't look at it as something strange.

Memorization and application are two separate things. A lot of brothers have good memories, but when it comes to applying, as soon as some trial or tribulation comes they are out the door. These are the weak men and weak women who can quote and find scriptures like firecrackers, the precepticons, but one little thing happens to them and they are gone. Most of them have not been through nothing; their life has been relatively smooth. The leadership sits back: he's all right with them precepts, but let's watch what he does when something bad happens to him. We are not wishing it, but according to the scriptures we know it is going to happen.

You know all these precepts, but you forget the precept Thou shalt not commit adultery. You have a precept for this and that, but when it comes to your winky wanky, the little head is bigger than the big head.

“But rejoice, inasmuch as ye are partakers of Christ’s sufferings”: when you go through bad things, rejoice, because you are a partaker of Christ's sufferings, “that, when his glory shall be revealed, ye may be glad also with exceeding joy.”

“If ye be reproached for the name of Christ, happy are ye”: if somebody is lying on you, slandering you, hating you because you are an Israelite, because the name of Christ is on you, happy are ye, “for the spirit of glory and of God resteth upon you”. When they attack us, as a whole or individually, we know it is the Holy Spirit on us. Oh, you said Christ, that's Greek; all right, Yahawashi; I still hate you.

“On their part he is evil spoken of, but on your part he is glorified”: on our part we are glorifying the spirit of God, the spirit of the Lord.

“But let none of you suffer as a murderer”: like the Florida father who met a woman on a dating site, and she came back with three men to rob him, and he was shot in the head begging for his life, telling them he had a five-year-old girl. What does that have to do with us? Some of you brothers are on dating apps, and God forbid you end up like that brother. There was a sister with us, sat right there with the head covering and the fringes, and an Edomite emailed with the receipts: he was paying her rent, and she was with two or three other men. A ho from hell, meeting men on dating apps. You never know.

“Or as a thief, or as an evildoer, or as a busybody in other men’s matters.” Brothers who teach online: do not get involved with gossip. Look at the woman who spent years slandering Jay-Z, and now that he is suing for defamation she has no evidence and is nowhere to be found. That is the same with the camps that slander with no evidence, and stupid people entertain it, because black people just love drama. Remember the man who said we had a sister murdered: when the cease and desist letter came he packed up and left the country.

precepts.why: Saying the same thing: “My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” Prepare your soul for temptation. The fiery trial is not strange; it is what comes to those who serve the Lord.

“He therefore that despiseth, despiseth not man, but God, who hath also given unto us his holy Spirit.” That is the mentality we all have to have when people are reproaching us for the name of Christ. It is not you that they hate; it is the spirit of God they see within you. That man and that woman have the Holy Spirit, and I can't stand it because I ain't got it. Oh, it's not hatred, it's correction: I wish you'd die. That's what they do.

sense.text: “Wherein ye greatly rejoice, though now for a season, if need be, ye are in heaviness through manifold temptations”: sometimes we are sad and depressed through manifold temptations. There is a lot of trouble coming into our lives.

“That the trial of your faith”: Christ is letting us know through Peter that it is the trying of your faith, “being much more precious than of gold that perisheth, though it be tried with fire, might be found unto praise and honour and glory at the appearing of Jesus Christ”. There is a purpose behind the manifold temptations, the manifold struggles.
“Whom having not seen, ye love”: we haven't seen Christ, but we love him, “yet believing, ye rejoice with joy unspeakable and full of glory”.
“Receiving the end of your faith, even the salvation of your souls.” That is what we want; that is what we are waiting on.

Battle fatigue is a term often used in class, and some use it out of context. Battle fatigue is when you are tired of obeying God, tired of keeping God's commandments. You'd rather be a ho, a drug addict or a drug dealer, or a homo, than keep yourself disciplined day after day and night after night. You are willing to lose salvation and destroy your family over battle fatigue, and we have seen it in here: I just want to be a ho, if only for a night.

“By faith Moses, when he was come to years, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh’s daughter; Choosing rather to suffer affliction with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season”. That is battle fatigue: when you want to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season, when you want to stop being obedient just for a little while and go into your sin.

Sisters say, oh, I'm suffering battle fatigue. Sister, do you know what battle fatigue is? You are in a fight, you are losing, and you are giving up. In this spiritual fight you are giving up on God, on his laws, his statutes, his commandments, his precepts.

precepts.why: The sin of battle fatigue is plain: “Whosoever committeth sin transgresseth also the law: for sin is the transgression of the law.” The pleasures of sin are breaking God's laws.

“That they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness.” Some of you suffer battle fatigue: you had pleasure in unrighteousness, in sin.

“But we are bound to give thanks alway to God for you, brethren beloved of the Lord, because God hath from the beginning chosen you to salvation through sanctification of the Spirit”. All of us who have been called are called to be sanctified, to receive the coming kingdom on earth.

sense.text: “The sower soweth the word.” We often talk about the four types of Israelites, and this is the time to discuss it again.

The first type: “And these are they by the way side, where the word is sown; but when they have heard, Satan cometh immediately, and taketh away the word that was sown in their hearts.” That is when you are teaching on the street, and the person you are teaching starts to get it, and a friend or a neighbour comes by and draws that person away. That is Satan, taking them away from hearing the truth.

The second type: “And these are they likewise which are sown on stony ground; who, when they have heard the word, immediately receive it with gladness”. That is some of you in here: you receive the word with gladness as soon as you hear the truth.

“And have no root in themselves”: you brothers and sisters that hear this truth gladly, some of you have no root, and that means you don't study the things we are teaching. You are not taking it seriously. Brothers put the class on and say, I watch class every day. A part of study is not just watching class: it is taking notes, then going over those notes when class is finished, rehearsing them: what does this verse mean, why did the Bishop or the deacons or the captains say this, let me go back to the video. That is building yourself up, applying what you have been taught; not cutting the class on while you walk around cooking, cleaning and mopping. You are not playing us; you are playing yourself. It is like people on fake diets, keto this and keto that, who won't go to the gym and order a Diet Coke with no ice with their five hamburgers. Then at the table or in the war room: I never heard that. We went over that last week. Check your notes.

“And so endure but for a time”: brothers and sisters like that will only endure for a time. It does not say how long; it is kept vague, a year, two, three, maybe five. “Afterward, when affliction or persecution ariseth for the word’s sake”: it will surely come. Remember: when you come to serve the Lord, prepare your soul. “Immediately they are offended”: you get offended and you leave, especially you precept brothers who don't apply nothing. As soon as a little affliction comes your way you are out the door, or you find an excuse: he looked at me wrong, she didn't say shalom to me, y'all don't have the spirit of Christ, I'm out. But it was really the affliction you were getting, and you don't want to say that, so you blame somebody else.

The third group: “And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word, And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches”.

“And the lusts of other things entering in”: that is so vague it can be anything. It is left vague because everybody in here is struggling with a different demon. We all battle with thirteen, as Christ said, and one of them is stronger than the others, and only you know which one it is, you and the Lord.

precepts.why:
What does it mean to have no root? “As ye have therefore received Christ Jesus the Lord, so walk ye in him: Rooted and built up in him, and stablished in the faith, as ye have been taught”. As ye have been taught: brothers and sisters, what we have been teaching you, for some of you years and for some months, you better hold on to it.

“Abounding therein with thanksgiving”: you have to abound in this truth, grow in this truth, have the fruits of the spirit, be rooted in Christ. And notice it says rooted and built up in him. A part of being built up is not just memorizing precepts. It means you have to go through hard times, in your family, at work, in your marriage, with your health; whatever it is, something is going to build you, and it is meant to build you.

The affliction and persecution that arise for the word's sake: “If ye be reproached for the name of Christ, happy are ye; for the spirit of glory and of God resteth upon you”. You are being reproached for the name of Christ, and that is a part of your affliction.

“But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another: for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Israel, till the Son of man be come.” That is the men out there in the highways and byways teaching: persecution arises for the word's sake.

The deceitfulness of riches. Some of you want to be rich, like the sister who wanted to go to England and become rich, or the one in Houston who was on America's Next Top Model and got hooked into a lesbian affair: all to be rich and famous. Where is she now? Nowhere, probably homeless.

“But they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare”: the wrong kind of temptation, “and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.” “For the love of money is the root of all evil”: money was your god. You wanted to be rich, you wanted to be famous.

“Which while some coveted after”: the Lord says thou shalt not covet, but you are coveting after what is not yours, which you are not getting lawfully, whether it's rape, robbery, murder or spreading your cheeks. OnlyFans: sisters who used to be with us are on OnlyFans right now, and brothers too out there. Y'all better repent. “They have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows”: that is the hurt.

“Why is earth and ashes proud?” Man is earth and ashes. “There is not a more wicked thing than a covetous man: for such an one setteth his own soul to sale”: there is nothing worse than a covetous man; he will sell his own soul. “Because while he liveth he casteth away his bowels”: while he lives he casts away his bowels, his rectum.

You want money so damn bad you'll do anything for it, like a crackhead. Back in the nineties, outside a store, a crackhead with no money was told she had to go down on a man's pit bull to get her crack, and she did it. You can't make this stuff up.

“Go not after thy lusts”: brothers, sisters, do not go after your lust. Examine yourself right now and think about what your lust is. “But refrain thyself from thine appetites”: refrain means discipline that spirit within you. Notice it puts lust and food together: some of you lust after chicken and hamburgers and grits, some of you lust after sex.

“If thou givest thy soul the desires that please her, she will make thee a laughingstock to thine enemies that malign thee.” If you give in to the temptation, whatever it is, little girls, little boys, animals. A brother just got out of jail: he drove five hours to meet a girl he met on Facebook who told him she was thirteen, age ain't nothing but a number, and who came out of the house but Chris Hansen. When lust is on you, common sense is gone. A brother's RV blew up because a goat rammed it; the brother was messing with that goat. A woman ran up the stairs of the old school in the middle of class asking Tyrone for the five dollars he owed her.

Everybody in here seems holier than thou, but some of the raunchiest and nastiest brothers have been here. There are people waiting for you to fall, and as soon as you fall the whole family knows. And when the brothers and sisters among us go out and do evil, who do they blame? IUIC. We don't claim that everybody here is perfect; Christ came for sinners. Everybody is dealing with something, but you have to overcome these things, and if you need help, come for counsel. If you don't control it, it is going to come out, and the ministry gets blamed.

“Giving no offence in any thing, that the ministry be not blamed”. Some of you brothers may have done things in your past, maybe statutory rape at seventeen with a fifteen-year-old, or worse, and when you are a sex offender you register, and some have stipulations not to be around children. We have kids upstairs, and we don't want to give nobody a reason to try to shut us down. We are not going to put your business out in the air, humiliate you or try to destroy you, but give us the heads-up.

That is what we are trying to avoid: we don't want the ministry blamed, and our first thing is to make sure this truth continues. You are trying to hide your sins, like the brother who said he couldn't come on the Sabbath because he was on a cruise, and when it was looked up it was an LGBT cruise: I didn't know until I got on. That's a damn lie. Some of y'all know what you are battling with. We are not trying to judge or condemn anybody; we are saying discipline those spirits more.

A brother who was put out of the school for beating his wife went months later to buy a prostitute who turned out to be a transvestite, and shot the person, and it was all over the news. He was not part of us, and they dug into his past to blame the ministry anyway. That is why you all have to bring those lusts under control, and second and third offenders will have to stay online and watch.

“Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth”: mortify means deaden, put to death. “Fornication”: those fornicating thoughts, deaden them. “Uncleanness”: sexual uncleanness. “Inordinate affection”: if you like little children, that is inordinate affection; she was fifteen and you're forty-five, what is wrong with you? Just stop it. “Evil concupiscence”: evil sexual desires, like pornography.

“And covetousness, which is idolatry”: what is your idol? It could be anything, money. Your rod is your idol: you want to bust a nut, and that is all you care about. When sex is your drive and your goal and you want to please your rod, that is your idol. In other camps that is all they talk about; one camp had their members stand up and say their school had the best vagina, and that is what we see in the Black Hebrew Israelite community.

sense.text:
“For a just man falleth seven times, and riseth up again”. As men in the flesh and sisters in the flesh we struggle and we fall at times; we understand that. The point is not staying down. You get knocked down in sin, get back up and start fighting all over again. Never give up.

“But the wicked shall fall into mischief”: the wicked that falls into mischief is the brother or sister that just gives in and gives up.

precepts.why:
“If thou faint in the day of adversity, thy strength is small.” To faint means you give up as soon as adversity comes your way. All that yelling we do, be strong in the Lord and in the power of his might, is BS with you, because you gave up.

Like the brother who couldn't stop whacking off and blamed us because he couldn't stop choking his chicken. If you have masturbation problems, don't blame us: pray and fast, get a wife. We got him a wife, and that wasn't good enough. These are demons, and some of you are dealing with these demons out here.

This goes with what we read in Ecclesiasticus 18, that giving in to your lust will make you a laughingstock to your enemies that malign you. “For I heard the defaming of many, fear on every side.” Many people try to defame us, on every side. “Report, say they, and we will report it”: tell us the story so that we can say it.

“All my familiars watched for my halting”: your familiars are your friends and family, and halting is falling. “Saying, Peradventure he will be enticed”: hopefully that nigga will give in to his temptation, “and we shall prevail against him, and we shall take our revenge on him”, because he is always correcting us about the Bible, about God's laws, and they hate that. As soon as he falls, they are happy.

sense.text: This is what Paul went through: “For Demas hath forsaken me, having loved this present world”. Demas was one of the servants in the truth, a disciple, and he gave up. “And is departed unto Thessalonica; Crescens to Galatia, Titus unto Dalmatia.” These are people who left Paul, left the ministry, and went back into the world. For how long it doesn't say, or whether they came back; we'll find out when Christ returns.
“Only Luke is with me.” “Take Mark, and bring him with thee”: Mark was Barnabas's nephew, “for he is profitable to me for the ministry.”

“And Tychicus have I sent to Ephesus. The cloke that I left at Troas with Carpus, when thou comest, bring with thee, and the books, but especially the parchments.” The work is still getting done today: a brother just came back from Ghana, and brothers are in Santo Domingo and Haiti right now. We need you brothers to step up in your growth and your understanding so you can be better utilized in this truth. But you have to get hold of your lusts. In the third-world countries there are prostitutes downstairs in the hotels waiting for Americans, and that is why you have to have a brother with you.

“Alexander the coppersmith did me much evil: the Lord reward him according to his works”. That was another man who was with Paul, as you read in the book of Acts, and turned on him. “For he hath greatly withstood our words.”

“At my first answer no man stood with me, but all men forsook me”: everybody that was with Paul left him, at the time of the amphitheatre when they cried out for Diana. There will be times, whether you travel in this truth or wherever you are, when it may feel like you are the last man standing. That is how Paul felt: everybody left me, what is going on here? “I pray God that it may not be laid to their charge.”

“Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me”. When your foundation is built on the rock, which is Christ, you are going to be all right. When your foundation is built on a man, you messed up, because men fall, make mistakes and err. At the old school there were about two hundred brothers who built their foundation on the men, the seven elders, and when those men stumbled and fell, those brothers went back out into the world. Only seven or eight remain.

“That by me the preaching might be fully known, and that all the Gentiles might hear”: the Gentiles are Israel. “And I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion”: the mouth of the lion is Emperor Nero.

precepts.why:
Paul quoted Elijah because Paul felt like he was the last man standing, and you do feel like that at times. “I say then, Hath God cast away his people?” That is the teaching of the Catholic Church: that God's new people is the church and the Israelites are done away with. That is a lie. Many church groups say God is looking for a spiritual Israel because real Israel was destroyed. That is a lie. “God forbid. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew”: foreknew means from the past, from the Old Testament.

“Wot ye not what the scripture saith of Elias? how he maketh intercession to God against Israel, saying, Lord, they have killed thy prophets, and digged down thine altars; and I am left alone, and they seek my life.” In the book of Kings, Jezebel was killing the prophets of God, and Obadiah hid them in caves by fifty. Elijah felt like he was the last man standing.

“But what saith the answer of God unto him? I have reserved to myself seven thousand men, who have not bowed the knee to the image of Baal.” That is why the Lord does not reveal our true numbers in this truth. So many watch us online, and behind each computer there is a whole bunch of people, in this city, the next state and the next countries. The Lord doesn't show us that, so we don't get big-headed.

“Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace.” That was in Paul's time, but it applies to us today too. Although you might feel like you are by yourself, the Lord says no, I have seven thousand men.

sense.text: “I therefore so run, not as uncertainly; so fight I, not as one that beateth the air”. In this truth it is like running a race, and your goal is to reach the finish line.

“But I keep under my body, and bring it into subjection”: mortify your members upon the earth; keep your body under, and bring it into subjection to God's laws. “Lest that by any means, when I have preached to others, I myself should be a castaway.”

There was a brother named Kenny who cursed out another brother like a dog for watching porn: stop looking at porn, it's the devil. Then he handed the Bishop his phone to show him a Batman trailer, and the last thing he had been looking at popped up: pornography. You don't want to be a hypocrite and be cast away. Get yourself right, and that will help your preaching and your teaching.

precepts.why: “There is one that is wise and teacheth many, and yet is unprofitable to himself.” Why is he unprofitable to himself? Because he is living his life as a hypocrite. None of us should fall into that. If you find yourself in that situation right now, repent right now and fix it. We have to learn to endure to the end.

sense.text:
“But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved.” To endure is to suffer something painful or difficult patiently: to undergo, go through, live through, face up to, handle, tolerate. We have to endure in this truth to the end.

But what does the end make reference to? There are two thoughts: the end is either the end of your current life, or the end is when Christ returns. And to endure to the end is not only until you die or until Christ returns; it goes into the affliction we are going to go through. They are going to kill some of us, and you have to endure the suffering, even being killed. You can't give up no matter what you go through. That is heavy, brothers and sisters: we have to make up our minds that the Lord might try me even unto death, to see if I will endure and take death for him.

precepts.why: Elisha had a double portion of the spirit of Elijah. “Now Elisha was fallen sick of his sickness whereof he died.” Imagine: he had a double portion of the Holy Spirit, and he fell sick, and he died of that sickness. Does that mean Elisha was a sinner? No. That is how the Lord chose to call him back. Did he endure to the end? Yes.

This is the woman who had seven sons. “After him was the third made a mocking stock: and when he was required, he put out his tongue, and that right soon, holding forth his hands manfully, And said courageously, These I had from heaven”: my hands and my tongue. “And for his laws I despise them”: for God's laws I despise my hands and my tongue. “And from him I hope to receive them again”: from the Almighty I hope to receive my hands and my tongue again. “Insomuch that the king, and they that were with him, marvelled at the young man’s courage, for that he nothing regarded the pains.”

“Now when this man was dead also, they tormented and mangled the fourth in like manner.” To mangle is to cut, bruise or hack with repeated blows: to batter, maim and mutilate. “So when he was ready to die he said thus, It is good, being put to death by men, to look for hope from God to be raised up again by him: as for thee, thou shalt have no resurrection to life.” That is what he said to the white man, the Greek: thou shalt have no resurrection to life.

Now the mother: “But she bowing herself toward him, laughing the cruel tyrant to scorn”: she laughed the Greeks to scorn. She “spake in her country language on this manner”: she spoke in Hebrew. “O my son, have pity upon me that bare thee nine months in my womb”, and she gave him suck three years, because our women used to breastfeed babies for three years; it ain't like today, six months and you're out.

She “nourished thee, and brought thee up unto this age, and endured the troubles of education.” She raised seven sons and endured the troubles of education. Sisters complain, it's hard, I can't do it; nobody says it's easy, but that's your job. It is easier to let the white man teach your child, and then when your son comes back an LGBT member you are confounded: why does my kid want to put on a dress? Because you gave your child to the white man rather than endure the troubles of education yourself.

“I beseech thee, my son, look upon the heaven and the earth, and all that is therein, and consider that God made them of things that were not”: that is heavy right there. “And so was mankind made likewise.” “Fear not this tormentor, but, being worthy of thy brethren, take thy death, that I may receive thee again in mercy with thy brethren.” She understood regeneration: you are going to come back, and I am going to be your mother again.

“And he sent, and beheaded John in the prison. And his head was brought in a charger, and given to the damsel: and she brought it to her mother.” They cut John the Baptist's head off. A charger is like the covered tray a restaurant brings your food on. These are the various people who endured to the end, and their end was death.

Still enduring to the end, in the context of death: “And they stoned Stephen, calling upon God, and saying, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit. And he kneeled down, and cried with a loud voice, Lord, lay not this sin to their charge. And when he had said this, he fell asleep.”

“And Saul was consenting unto his death. And at that time there was a great persecution against the church which was at Jerusalem”. That is the part to get to. We are not in Jerusalem today, but the persecution will return.

“And they were all scattered abroad throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except the apostles. And devout men carried Stephen to his burial, and made great lamentation over him.” When you feel like you are the last man standing, you will survive if your faith is built on Christ. Imagine how they felt: they were all scattered abroad. We like to think we are always going to be together, but by what we read in 2 Esdras 16 there will be persecution; this school might not be here no more, and every man and every woman will have to stand on their own. Last man standing. That is going to be proving time, trying time.

We read Acts like it is some nice history. But “whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” Paul is saying the things you read about will happen again.

As we read at the beginning of the class: “For there shall be in every place, and in the next cities, a great insurrection upon those that fear the Lord.” That is prophecy. The persecution that came on the church at Jerusalem will return. Do you think the white man is going to let Israel just grow like this and sit back and twiddle his thumbs? No. That is why the ADL, the SPLC, AIPAC and Canary Mission are all behind the scenes putting laws in place, hate speech. They put us number three on the hate group list, and all we do is read the Bible. We ain't burned no cross on a lawn, we ain't set no bombs. But when we speak the words of the Bible, things happen.

Enduring to the end in terms of death: “Now about that time Herod the king stretched forth his hands to vex certain of the church. And he killed James the brother of John with the sword. And because he saw it pleased the Jews, he proceeded further to take Peter also.” Why did he take Peter? To make Peter a public example, to put fear in all the rest of the believers in Christ so that they would stop teaching. That was his plan, his agenda. It didn't work out that way.
